name: Accessibility Audit Lite
blurb: contrast, focus order and missing labels in pasted HTML
intro: Reads pasted HTML without rendering it and reports what WCAG 2.2 checks can decide from the markup: text contrast from inline styles and simple <style> rules, fields, buttons, links and images without a name, keyboard reach, the Tab order, headings, language and zoom.

usage: Pass the markup as html (a string), level AA or AAA, and the page's default text colour and background as CSS colours. It returns error and warning counts, an Issues table (severity, problem, WCAG criterion, line, element, why, fix), the Tab focus order with each stop's accessible name, and every text node's contrast ratio. Use it to review generated or pasted markup before shipping; it does not render, so pair it with axe or Lighthouse on the live page.
sources: W3C WCAG 2.2 (success criteria 1.1.1, 1.3.1, 1.4.3, 1.4.4, 1.4.6, 2.1.1, 2.4.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.4, 2.4.7, 3.1.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2) and its definitions of relative luminance, contrast ratio and large text
